stages.reference: Study the first small stresses forming inside the same frost-covered ice established by the unbroken stage. A few fine hairline fractures begin to branch under the surface and gently whiten their immediate surroundings; most of the blue-gray translucent sheet still carries uninterrupted cold depth. Slight clouding from trapped air should grow alongside the cracks rather than replacing the material. This is a restrained progression from stage zero, not a new species of ice or a broken window. Use soft neutral light and natural unevenness, with fracture lines that feel caused by temperature and pressure. Avoid broad opaque white veins, abrupt black fissures, ornamental symmetry, glitter, sharp glass shards or a snow-covered landscape. Keep the underlying ice familiar and largely intact.
